sections.label: Amendment to un-commenced legislation
sections.summary: An amendment to be introduced at Committee stage would amend un-commenced legislation so common law developments are not abolished when it comes into force.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: One amendment, which I will seek to introduce at the Committee stage, is for the purpose of amending un-commenced legislation so that common law developments are not abolished once the legislation is brought into force.

sections.label: Deputy Chairman appointments no longer mandatory
sections.summary: Clauses 4 and 7 amend each respective Act so appointing a Deputy Chairman for the NAC or SSC is no longer mandatory.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clauses 4 and 7 of the Bill amend each respective Act such that it will no longer be mandatory to appoint a Deputy Chairman for the National Arts Council (NAC) or the Singapore Sports Council (SSC).

sections.label: Amendment to section 26D wilful blindness
sections.summary: An amendment to section 26D will be proposed to preserve the current law, including the extended conception of wilful blindness with its three elements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This outcome would be contrary to the policy intention of section 26D, which is to codify the law, rather than to change or narrow the position under the law.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: I will, therefore, be proposing an amendment to section 26D to preserve the position under the current law, which includes the "extended conception of wilful blindness".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: For completeness, Mr Deputy Speaker, I should point out that the Court of Appeal had explained that there are three elements to the "extended conception of wilful blindness", and these are, namely: one, the accused must have had a clear, grounded and targeted suspicion of the fact to which he is said to have been wilfully blind; two, there must have been reasonable means of inquiry available to the accused person, which, if taken, would have led him to discovery of the truth, at least in the context of the fact of possession; and three, the accused must have deliberately refused to pursue the reasonable means of inquiry so as to avoid having such negative legal consequences as might arise in connection with his knowing that fact.

sections.label: SCORE financial year amendment
sections.summary: Clause 6 amends the SCORE Act so SCORE's financial year runs 1 April to 31 March, aligning it with the Government and other MHA agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Bill amends the Singapore Corporation of Rehabilitative Enterprises (SCORE) Act, such that SCORE’s financial year will run from 1 April of each year to 31 March of the following year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This will align SCORE’s financial year with that of the Government and other Ministry of Home Affairs agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, there are two amendments, as I have outlined earlier, to clause 5, as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.
